VPG0003.title: Journal history below 75% of SLA after a sync
VPG0003.meaning: 'VPG has low journal history' (Warning). The configured Journal History is at least 1 hour, but the journal holds less than 75% of it. This is normally because a sync (initial, delta or bitmap) moved older data out of the journal without adding new checkpoints. Zerto says the alert resolves automatically once the history refills.
VPG0003.fix: If {vpg} is in a sync or has recently finished one, no action is needed: history refills over time. If the alert keeps coming back, find what keeps forcing syncs (WAN drops, ZVM0002 VRA disconnects, recovery storage errors) and fix that.
VPG0003.caution: Don't Force Sync to clear it: a sync removes more checkpoints. Until history rebuilds, recovery is limited to the checkpoints still in the journal. If Replication Pause Time is set, a sync that is about to remove the last checkpoints pauses first (VPG0007) so a clone can be taken.
VPG0003.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0003.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-27); KB 000003880 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/3880.html; Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Forcing_Sync_VPG.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Policies.htm

VPG0004.title: Journal history critically low after a sync
VPG0004.meaning: 'VPG has low journal history' (Error). Journal history has fallen well below the SLA after a sync, such as a bitmap sync. Zerto's thresholds: under 75% of the configured history when 1 hour or less is configured; under 75% or under one hour when more than 1 hour is configured. Zerto also lists an MTU too large for a VPN path as a cause. The alert resolves automatically once the history refills.
VPG0004.fix: Handle it as VPG0003. If it recurs on many VPGs to the same peer, test the path MTU the way Zerto describes (ping -f -l starting at 1500 and dropping by 10 until the 'needs to be fragmented' reply stops) and fix the network path.
VPG0004.caution: Few recovery points remain: if a disaster happens now, recovery is only possible to the checkpoints still in the journal. Avoid Force Sync and Pause/Resume; the syncs they trigger add no new checkpoints while older ones keep aging out.
VPG0004.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0004.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-27); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Statuses.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Forcing_Sync_VPG.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Resuming_Protection_of_VPGs.htm

VPG0005.title: VPG in an unrecoverable error state
VPG0005.meaning: 'VPG in error state' (Error). Zerto reports an error it cannot fix. The message says the VPG must be deleted, and the documented resolution is to delete it and reprotect the VMs.
VPG0005.fix: Open a Zerto Support case and tell the customer before changing anything. If deletion is confirmed as the only path, use MORE > Delete with 'Keep the recovery disks at the peer site' checked (event EV0040 in Monitoring > Events records where the disks are kept), then re-create the VPG using them as preseeded volumes so it runs a delta sync. On vCD sites, first place the disks in the ZORG's preseed folder (set in ZCM) on a datastore enabled for Preseed in Configure Provider vDCs, with all of a VM's preseeded disks on the same datastore.
VPG0005.caution: Deleting the VPG discards the journal: every checkpoint is lost, and the VMs are unprotected until the new VPG finishes syncing. Leaving 'Keep the recovery disks' unchecked deletes the replicas and forces a full initial sync over the WAN.
VPG0005.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0005.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Deleting_a_VPG.htm (EV0040), https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Enable_Protection_to_Continue_When_Journal_Recovery_Storage_Unavailable.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Edit-Recovery-for-vCD-Recovery-Environments.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/ConfigureProvidervDCs.htm

VPG0006.title: VPG needs configuration (missing or invalid settings)
VPG0006.meaning: 'VPG missing configuration details' (Error; the VPG status is Needs Configuration). Typical causes: a VM or volume was added with no matching recovery storage; an Org vDC network was removed at the recovery site; VPG settings were not updated during a site or vCenter disconnection; or a Failover/Move was done without reverse protection.
VPG0006.fix: If a site or vCenter/vCD disconnection caused it, restore connectivity first. Otherwise open Edit VPG on {vpg}, find the flagged step, and pick a storage policy for newly added VMs or volumes, or an existing Org vDC network to replace a removed one. If it follows a Failover/Move without reverse protection, leave it until the customer decides whether to reprotect or remove the VPG.
VPG0006.caution: Reprotecting after a Move without reverse protection needs a full initial sync, because the original disks were deleted. Don't enlarge a protected VM's disk while it is in a test or recovery state; Zerto says this can leave the VPG in Needs Configuration until the VM is removed or the VPG is rebuilt.
VPG0006.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0006.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Reverse_Protection_Not_Specified.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Committing_the_Move_Operation.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/The_Test_Failover_Process.htm

VPG0007.title: Sync paused before it wipes the last checkpoints
VPG0007.meaning: 'VPG replication paused' (Error). A running sync was about to remove the last checkpoints (200 or fewer remained). Because Replication Pause Time is set (Site Settings > Policies), Zerto pauses replication for that time so a recovery point can be preserved, then resumes automatically.
VPG0007.fix: Act before the pause expires. If the customer needs a guaranteed recovery point, run an Offsite Clone of {vpg} to the latest checkpoint (VPGs tab > three-dot menu > Offsite Clone); on a vCD recovery site the clone is created in vCenter and must be imported into vCD. Then find out why the sync is taking so long (WAN, journal too small, recovery storage).
VPG0007.caution: When replication resumes, the sync can remove every remaining checkpoint, and no failover is possible until it completes. Clones are unprotected copies on recovery storage that keep the source VMs' MAC/IP settings; Zerto notes a leftover clone can stop VMs powering on in a later failover (MAC/IP conflict), so delete clones as soon as they are no longer needed.
VPG0007.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0007.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Cloning_VPG_to_the_Recovery_Site.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/The_Clone_Operation.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Policies.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/The_Failover_Live_Process.htm

VPG0008.title: Failover/Move rollback did not finish cleanup
VPG0008.meaning: 'VPG rollback failed' (Error). Rolling back a Failover/Move before commit left incomplete tasks. Zerto lists three causes: the ZVM-to-vCenter (hypervisor manager) link is down, the ZVM-to-VRA link is down, or an internal error occurred.
VPG0008.fix: Wait several minutes for the ZVM to retry. If the alert persists, check ZVM-vCenter/vCD and ZVM-VRA connectivity (ports 4005/4006/4009), then open a Zerto Support case.
VPG0008.caution: Don't delete Zerto-created recovery VMs or VRA-attached disks by hand to clean up; they can be the replica. Let the ZVM or Zerto Support do the cleanup.
VPG0008.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0008.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); KB 000004787 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4787.html

VPG0009.title: VPG RPO is 15-25% over its target
VPG0009.meaning: 'VPG target RPO exceeded' (Warning). Writes are not being replicated fast enough: the time since the last journal checkpoint is 15-25% above the VPG's Target RPO Alert. Zerto lists four causes: an IO burst, a VRA bottleneck, a slow network, or slow recovery storage. For inbound customer VPGs both sides matter. The protected side is the customer's: their VRAs, their WAN and their bandwidth throttle. Their traffic reaches the provider through their Zerto Cloud Connector (ZCC), a provider-hosted VM on the cloud side, and the recovery side is the provider's VRAs and storage. At 25% or more over target it escalates to VPG0010.
VPG0009.fix: Open {vpg} > Performance graphs: an IOPS/Throughput spike that is already easing is a burst, so watch it recover. A flat ceiling on WAN Traffic (compressed, so normally below Throughput) points to bandwidth: the WAN, the protected site's throttle (Site Settings > Performance and Throttling; the customer's setting on inbound VPGs) or the customer's ZCC on the provider's side. Otherwise check the recovery side and the VRAs: VRA0059 high storage latency (40 ms default), journal and recovery datastore free space, and ZVM0002/VRA0063 on the VRAs {vpg} uses.
VPG0009.caution: Don't use Force Sync or Pause/Resume to 'kick' the VPG: syncs add no new checkpoints and let old ones age out, and Resume usually triggers a bitmap sync. Raising a VRA's RAM or vCPU powers that VRA off, which affects every VPG on it and leaves them to resync; KB 3532 says to do it only after a performance review. On inbound VPGs the bandwidth throttle is the customer's setting, so coordinate any change with them.
VPG0009.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0009.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VRA0059.htm (same bundle, updated 2025-10-27); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/ZCC0002.htm (same bundle, updated 2025-10-25); KB 000003532 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/3532.html; Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Monitoring_a_Single_VPG.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/PerformanceandThrottling.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/EditVRA.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Forcing_Sync_VPG.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Resuming_Protection_of_VPGs.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/From_vCD_to_vCD_Define_Replication.htm (WAN compression on by default to vCD); ZCM Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/Design_Considerations_for_DRaaS.htm (ZCC installed on the cloud side)

VPG0010.title: VPG RPO is 25% or more over its target
VPG0010.meaning: 'VPG target RPO exceeded' (Error). Same mechanism as VPG0009, but RPO is 25% or more over the Target RPO Alert, so the newest recovery point keeps getting older. When the RPO recovers, Zerto logs a 'meeting configured RPO' event.
VPG0010.fix: Triage as for VPG0009, and confirm the journal datastore has at least min(30 GB, 15%) free (below that, journal writes are blocked). If {vpg} is stuck in a bitmap or delta sync and ZVM0002 (ports 4006/4009) names a provider VRA it uses (recovery side for inbound VPGs, either side for provider-to-provider), compare that VRA's subnet mask with the other VRAs on its gateway. If it differs (for example a /24 on a /23 network, which breaks ZVM-VRA comms), correct only the mask in Setup > VRAs > Actions > Edit.
VPG0010.caution: The VPG0009 cautions apply. A sync that outlasts the journal history can remove every checkpoint, so escalate early; a configured Replication Pause Time pauses the sync first (VPG0007), but don't count on the last few checkpoints being kept. Edit VRA changes affect every VPG on that VRA: change only the subnet mask (changing RAM or vCPU powers the VRA off), and only while the VRA is powered on, because per KB 4499 a change made while it is off reaches vCenter but not Zerto and the VRA never reconnects.
VPG0010.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0010.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0007.htm (same bundle); KB 000003532 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/3532.html; KB 000004787 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4787.html; KB 000004499 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4499.html (All versions, updated 2021-02-04); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Statuses.htm ('all the checkpoints in the journal can be lost'), https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Journal_Sizing.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/EditVRA.htm; Journal Sizing BP https://help.zerto.com/bundle/BP.Journal.Sizing.HTML/page/Journal_Overview_Sizing_and_Best_Practice.htm; VRA mask-mismatch check = provider field experience

VPG0011.title: VPG has never been failover-tested
VPG0011.meaning: 'VPG test overdue' (Warning). The VPG's Test Frequency Reminder has passed and the VPG has never been tested. It is a housekeeping and compliance alert, not a replication fault.
VPG0011.fix: Tell the customer or account owner and schedule a test: Failover > Test in the Zerto UI (either site can start it), using an isolated test network. Verify the VMs, then Stop the test and record the result.
VPG0011.caution: Use Failover Test, never Failover Live or Move. Replication continues during the test. Don't snapshot, delete, migrate or change the disks of the test VMs; Zerto says a snapshot corrupts them. Test VMs start with production IPs by default, so give them different IPs or an isolated network.
VPG0011.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0011.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/StartingFailoverTest.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/What_Happens_After_Starting_a_Test.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/The_Test_Failover_Process.htm

VPG0012.title: VPG's last successful test is older than its test frequency
VPG0012.meaning: 'VPG test overdue' (Warning). The last successful failover test is older than the VPG's Test Frequency Reminder. It is a housekeeping and compliance alert, not a replication fault.
VPG0012.fix: Tell the customer or account owner and schedule a test: Failover > Test, using an isolated test network. Verify the VMs, then Stop the test and record the result.
VPG0012.caution: Use Failover Test, never Failover Live or Move. Replication continues during the test. Don't snapshot, delete, migrate or change the disks of the test VMs, and keep test VMs on an isolated network or different IPs.
VPG0012.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0012.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/StartingFailoverTest.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/What_Happens_After_Starting_a_Test.htm

VPG0014.title: Failover/Move is waiting for commit or rollback
VPG0014.meaning: 'VPG waiting for commit or rollback' (Warning). A Failover Live or Move ran and is in its 'Before commit' stage. Someone must either Commit (finalize) or Roll back (abort). The operation's commit policy (the site default from Site Settings > Policies unless it was changed when the operation was started) may do this automatically when its timeout expires.
VPG0014.fix: Find the operation under {vpg} > Running Tasks, confirm with the customer or incident owner whether to Commit or Roll back, then do it from that task. Treat any timeout as a deadline: the operation can auto-commit or auto-roll back when it expires, and Site Settings > Policies (Failover/Move Commit Policy, Default Timeout) shows only the site default, not the policy this operation was started with.
VPG0014.caution: Never choose for the customer. Commit finalizes the operation. A Move removes the source VMs unless Keep Source VMs was chosen, and without reverse protection it deletes the source disks, so reprotecting later needs a full initial sync. A Failover with reverse protection powers off and removes the source VMs. Rollback aborts the operation, and the recovered VMs go away.
VPG0014.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0014.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Policies.htm ('can be changed when defining a failover or move operation'), https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Monitoring_a_Single_VPG.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/The_Failover_Live_Process.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Committing_the_Move_Operation.htm

VPG0017.title: VPG protection was paused by a user
VPG0017.meaning: 'VPG protection paused' (Warning). Someone clicked Pause, for example to free WAN bandwidth. The VPG can still be recovered to the last checkpoint written before the pause, but no new checkpoints are written while paused, so RPO keeps growing.
VPG0017.fix: Find who paused {vpg} and why (Monitoring > Events); it may be the customer or planned maintenance. When it is safe, select the VPG > MORE > Resume.
VPG0017.caution: Resuming will most likely trigger a bitmap sync, with no new checkpoints until it completes. Zerto recommends adding a checkpoint immediately before any future pause.
VPG0017.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0017.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Pausing_and_Resuming_the_Protection_of_a_VPG.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Resuming_Protection_of_VPGs.htm

VPG0018.title: VMs have no valid recovery storage policy in the Org vDC
VPG0018.meaning: 'VMs in VPG not configured with a storage policy' (Error). The VPG replicates to an Org vDC, but some of its VMs have no storage policy, or no enabled storage policy in that Org vDC contains their datastores. The original policy is no longer available.
VPG0018.fix: Have a provider vCD admin make an enabled storage policy on the Org vDC cover the VMs' datastores again: re-enable or re-add the original policy, or put its datastores back. Only if that is impossible, agree a replacement policy with the customer and edit the affected VMs in {vpg}.
VPG0018.caution: Choosing a different storage policy or datastore moves the recovery volumes; Zerto states that a datastore change puts the VPG through an initial sync.
VPG0018.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0018.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Managing_Protection_When_the_Recovery_Datastore_Will_Be_Unavailable_Datastore_Maintenance.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Statuses.htm

VPG0019.title: Recovery storage policy disabled in the Org vDC
VPG0019.meaning: 'VPG recovery storage policy disabled' (Error). A storage policy that VPGs use for recovery was disabled in the Org vDC. Zerto states that these VPGs cannot be recovered.
VPG0019.fix: In vCD, re-enable the storage policy on the Org vDC. If the disable was intentional, plan a replacement policy with the customer.
VPG0019.caution: Until the policy is re-enabled, these VPGs cannot be recovered. Moving VPGs to another policy moves their recovery volumes and forces initial syncs, so treat that as a last resort.
VPG0019.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0019.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Managing_Protection_When_the_Recovery_Datastore_Will_Be_Unavailable_Datastore_Maintenance.htm

VPG0020.title: Recovery storage policy missing from the Org vDC
VPG0020.meaning: 'VPG recovery storage policy not found' (Error). A storage policy (identified by its ID) that VPGs use is no longer found in the Org vDC, and no available policy includes the relevant datastores. Zerto states that these VPGs cannot be recovered.
VPG0020.fix: Have a provider vCD admin add the storage policy back to the Org vDC, or enable an existing policy that contains the relevant datastores.
VPG0020.caution: Until this is fixed, these VPGs cannot be recovered. Repointing VPGs to another policy moves recovery volumes and forces initial syncs, so treat it as a last resort.
VPG0020.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0020.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Managing_Protection_When_the_Recovery_Datastore_Will_Be_Unavailable_Datastore_Maintenance.htm

VPG0021.title: Recovery storage policy missing from the Provider vDC
VPG0021.meaning: 'VPG recovery storage policy not found' (Error). A storage policy that VPGs use is no longer found in the Provider vDC, and no available policy includes the relevant datastores. Zerto states that these VPGs cannot be recovered.
VPG0021.fix: Have a provider vCD admin add the storage policy back to the Provider vDC (and to the Org vDC if needed), or enable an existing policy that contains the relevant datastores.
VPG0021.caution: Until this is fixed, these VPGs cannot be recovered. Provider vDC changes affect every Org vDC and tenant on it, so plan them. Repointing VPGs to another policy forces initial syncs.
VPG0021.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0021.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Managing_Protection_When_the_Recovery_Datastore_Will_Be_Unavailable_Datastore_Maintenance.htm

VPG0022.title: Recovery storage policy disabled in the Provider vDC
VPG0022.meaning: 'VPG recovery storage policy disabled' (Error). A storage policy that VPGs use was disabled in the Provider vDC. Zerto states that these VPGs cannot be recovered.
VPG0022.fix: Have a provider vCD admin re-enable the storage policy on the Provider vDC. If the disable was intentional, plan a replacement policy with the affected customers.
VPG0022.caution: Until the policy is re-enabled, these VPGs cannot be recovered. Provider vDC changes affect every Org vDC and tenant on it. Repointing VPGs to another policy forces initial syncs.
VPG0022.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0022.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Managing_Protection_When_the_Recovery_Datastore_Will_Be_Unavailable_Datastore_Maintenance.htm

VPG0023.title: Storage policy missing in vCenter (Zerto docs conflict)
VPG0023.meaning: Error. The Zerto 8.5 guide defines it as: a storage policy in the Provider vDC is not found in the underlying vCenter even though VPGs use it, so those VPGs cannot be recovered (vCenter alarm RecoveryVcenterStoragePolicyMissing). The current 9.5-10.9 page keeps that alarm name but shows different text ('No connection to Extension Service', a vCD AMQP issue), so the 10.x meaning is unconfirmed.
VPG0023.fix: Read the alert text. If it names a missing storage policy, have the vCenter and vCD admins restore the vCenter VM storage policy that backs that Provider vDC policy; if it mentions the extension service, check ZVM-vCD connectivity. If it is unclear, open a Zerto Support case.
VPG0023.caution: Don't repoint VPGs to another storage policy as a first step; moving recovery volumes forces initial syncs.
VPG0023.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0023.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25; page content inconsistent); https://s3.amazonaws.com/zertodownload_docs/8.5_Latest/Guide%20to%20Alarms,%20Alerts%20and%20Events.pdf (Zerto's Alarms, Alerts and Events All Environments Rev02, 8.5, May 2021, p.60)

VPG0024.title: Recovery storage policy lost the datastores in use
VPG0024.meaning: 'VPG storage policy does not include active datastores' (Error). The VPG replicates to an Org vDC, but it cannot be recovered because datastores that hold its volumes were removed from the recovery storage policy.
VPG0024.fix: Add the datastores back to the storage policy; this is Zerto's first resolution. Only if that is impossible, change the affected VMs' storage in {vpg} with the customer's agreement.
VPG0024.caution: Until this is fixed, the VPG cannot be recovered. The fallback moves volumes and forces an initial sync.
VPG0024.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0024.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Statuses.htm

VPG0025.title: vApp networks have no recovery network mapping
VPG0025.meaning: 'vCD vApp network mapping not defined' (Warning). The VPG protects a vApp whose vApp networks connect to Org vDC networks that have no mapping defined. The NICs on those networks will be disconnected on failover.
VPG0025.fix: Edit {vpg} and configure network mapping for every network listed in the alert, for both failover and test. Agree the target networks with the customer.
VPG0025.caution: Until the networks are mapped, a failover brings the vApp up with disconnected NICs.
VPG0025.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0025.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25)

VPG0026.title: VPG's ZCM service profile no longer exists
VPG0026.meaning: 'VPG recovery storage profile changed' (Warning). The cloud provider (in ZCM) changed or removed the ZCM service profile that set this VPG's SLA. The VPG keeps its existing SLA values, such as journal history and the test reminder, until it is edited to use a valid profile.
VPG0026.fix: In ZCM, check Service Profiles and the profiles assigned to the ZORG (Organizations > {zorg} > Service Profiles). Then edit {vpg} to select a valid profile, agreeing the SLA with the customer.
VPG0026.caution: A profile with a shorter Journal History drops older checkpoints, and smaller journal limits shrink history. ZCM won't let you edit or remove a profile that a VPG uses, so create a new one instead.
VPG0026.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0026.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); ZCM Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/AddServiceProfile.1.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/ZORGServiceProfiles.htm

VPG0027.title: Some VMs in the VPG are no longer protected
VPG0027.meaning: 'VPG includes VMs that are no longer protected' (Warning). One or more VMs dropped out of protection, for example because the VRA on the VM's host was removed or the VM moved to a host without a VRA (see the VRA0001 'host has no VRA' alerts). It applies on the protected side: a provider site for provider-protected VPGs, or the customer's site for inbound VPGs.
VPG0027.fix: Find {vm}'s current host. vMotion the VM back to a host with a VRA, or install a VRA on that host; for inbound VPGs this is done on the customer's protected site.
VPG0027.caution: Zerto's third option, removing the VM from the VPG, means it can no longer be recovered; if you must remove it, answer Yes to keep its replica disks. Moving the VM back to a host with a VRA triggers a delta sync.
VPG0027.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0027.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Statuses.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Removing_Virtual_Machines_from_a_VPG.htm

VPG0028.title: Org vDC network mapping in the VPG is corrupted
VPG0028.meaning: 'Corrupted Org vDC network mapping' (Error). The Org vDC network mapping stored in the VPG for the listed networks has become corrupted.
VPG0028.fix: Edit {vpg} and re-select the Org vDC network mapping for the listed networks.
VPG0028.caution: Confirm the intended target networks with the customer before saving.
VPG0028.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0028.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25)

VPG0035.title: VPG's protected-side resources aren't assigned to its ZORG
VPG0035.meaning: 'VPG protected resources not in ZORG' (Warning). The VPG is tagged to a ZORG, but its protected VMs use resources that ZCM has not assigned to that ZORG: on a vCD site this is the vCD organization; on a vSphere site it is the resource pool, datastores or networks. KB 4340 ties this to setups where both the protected and recovery ZVMs are managed by ZCM (ICDR), such as provider-to-provider VPGs or VPGs protected from a provider site after a failover or move. It is not expected for VPGs protected from a customer-owned site. The 'resources:' list in the alert names what is outside the ZORG.
VPG0035.fix: Read the 'resources:' list in the alert. A provider ZCM admin then adds the missing resource: ZCM > Organizations > {zorg} > vCD Cloud Resources > ADD the protected VMs' vCD organization (on a vSphere site, vCenter Cloud Resources > ADD for the resource pool, datastores and networks). The alert clears once all are assigned; if {vpg} is tagged to the wrong ZORG, correct the ZORG in Edit VPG instead.
VPG0035.caution: ZORG resources are tenant boundaries. Each vCD org, and each resource pool, can belong to only one ZORG, so confirm the org belongs to this customer before adding it; if it already belongs to another ZORG, the VPG's ZORG is what's wrong. Only provider (ZCM) admins can change ZORG resources; tenants cannot. On a vCD site, the underlying vCenter resources cannot be used for a ZORG. Don't delete and re-create the VPG to clear the alert: that discards the journal and forces a new sync of the whole VPG.
VPG0035.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0035.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); KB 000004340 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4340.html; KB 000004197 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4197.html; ZCM Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/Adding_and_Editing_vCD_Resources.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/Making_VC_Server_Resources_Available_to_the_ZORG.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/vCDCloudResources.htm

VPG0036.title: VPG's recovery-side resources aren't assigned to its ZORG
VPG0036.meaning: 'VPG recovery resources not in ZORG' (Warning). The VPG is tagged to a ZORG, but the recovery resources it uses are not in that ZORG's ZCM resources. For inbound customer VPGs into vCD, this means the vCD organization of the target Org vDC; adding an org in ZCM brings in all of its Org vDCs. On a vSphere cloud site, it means the recovery resource pool, datastores or networks. Typical causes are that the org was never added to the ZORG, was later removed from it, or that the VPG carries the wrong ZORG. The 'resources:' list in the alert names the offending resources.
VPG0036.fix: Read the 'resources:' list. A provider ZCM admin adds the missing recovery resource: ZCM > Organizations > {zorg} > vCD Cloud Resources > ADD the recovery vCD organization (vSphere sites: vCenter Cloud Resources > ADD). If {vpg} carries the wrong ZORG, correct it in Edit VPG with the customer's agreement.
VPG0036.caution: Each vCD org and each resource pool can belong to only one ZORG. Verify ownership before adding, because a ZORG's resources are what that tenant can recover into. Zerto cannot change the recovery Org vDC of an existing VPG; re-targeting means delete and re-create, which loses the journal and needs a new initial sync (a full copy over the WAN unless the kept recovery disks can be reused as preseeded volumes). Fix it in ZCM instead. Changing a VM's recovery storage instead of fixing ZCM forces an initial sync of those volumes.
VPG0036.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0036.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); KB 000004340 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4340.html; ZCM Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/Adding_and_Editing_vCD_Resources.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/vCDCloudResources.htm; Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Editing_a_VPG.htm ('You cannot change a recovery Org vDC for an existing VPG'), https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Enable_Protection_to_Continue_When_Journal_Recovery_Storage_Unavailable.htm (keep disks + preseed = Delta Sync) and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Statuses.htm

VPG0037.title: Journal too small: history under 75% of SLA
VPG0037.meaning: 'Journal history is compromised' (Warning). The VPG has been protected long enough to hold its full history, but the journal hit its Journal Size Hard Limit. Zerto is therefore moving data to the recovery disks, and history has fallen below 75% of the configured Journal History. Zerto's stated resolution is to raise the hard limit manually.
VPG0037.fix: Check whether the customer's change rate rose and confirm journal-datastore space in Setup > Datastores. Then raise the Journal Size Hard Limit on each affected VM (Edit VPG > Replication > VM Settings). If {vpg} uses a non-Custom ZCM service profile, a provider ZCM admin adds one with a larger hard limit and the same or longer Journal History, assigns it to the ZORG (Organizations > {zorg} > Service Profiles), and {vpg} is edited to select it, agreed with the customer.
VPG0037.caution: The VRA0039 cautions apply: a sync may follow, larger journals consume recovery storage, and a journal datastore below min(30 GB, 15%) free blocks journal writes for every VPG on it. Never lower Journal History to meet the SLA; that discards checkpoints. After a service-profile switch, check each VM's journal limits in VM Settings.
VPG0037.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0037.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Journal_Sizing.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/To_VCD_Define_Replication.htm; ZCM Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/AddServiceProfile.1.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/ZORGServiceProfiles.htm; Journal Sizing BP https://help.zerto.com/bundle/BP.Journal.Sizing.HTML/page/Journal_Overview_Sizing_and_Best_Practice.htm

VPG0038.title: Journal too small: history under one hour
VPG0038.meaning: 'Journal history is compromised' (Error). Same cause as VPG0037: the journal is at its hard limit. History has now dropped below one hour, or below 45 minutes when only one hour is configured.
VPG0038.fix: Treat as urgent and handle as VPG0037: confirm journal-datastore space in Setup > Datastores, then raise the Journal Size Hard Limit on each affected VM (Edit VPG > Replication > VM Settings). If {vpg} uses a non-Custom ZCM service profile, in-use profiles can't be edited, so a provider ZCM admin adds one with a larger hard limit and the same or longer Journal History, assigns it to the ZORG (Organizations > {zorg} > Service Profiles), and {vpg} is edited to select it, agreed with the customer.
VPG0038.caution: Less than an hour of recovery points remains. Never lower Journal History or the hard limit, and avoid Force Sync and Pause/Resume. Raising the hard limit is still the documented fix, but Zerto lists journal size changes as a sync trigger and no new checkpoints are written during a sync, so make the change once per VM and watch history recover. Larger journals consume recovery storage, and the min(30 GB, 15%) free-space rule applies. After a service-profile switch, check each VM's journal limits in VM Settings.
VPG0038.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0038.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Journal_Sizing.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Synchronization_Triggers.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Statuses.htm; ZCM Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/AddServiceProfile.1.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/ZORGServiceProfiles.htm

VPG0040.title: Protected VMs' hardware version unsupported at the recovery site
VPG0040.meaning: 'Virtual machine hardware mismatch with recovery site' (Error). The protected VMs' virtual hardware version is newer than the recovery hosts support, so the VMs cannot be powered on after recovery. Zerto states that the VPG cannot be recovered.
VPG0040.fix: Compare {vm}'s virtual hardware version with the highest version the recovery cluster's ESXi build supports. Zerto's fix is to upgrade the recovery hosts, so plan an ESXi upgrade of that cluster, and on vCD also check that the Provider vDC's highest supported hardware version covers it. Until then, tell the customer these VMs will not power on after a failover and ask them not to raise VM hardware versions beyond what the cloud supports.
VPG0040.caution: This is a live DR gap: the affected VMs will not boot in a failover until it is fixed. Zerto's other option, a different recovery host, means a different Org vDC on vCD, which needs the VPG deleted and re-created: the journal is lost and a new initial sync runs. Downgrading VM hardware is a customer-side VMware change, not a Zerto setting.
VPG0040.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0040.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Editing_a_VPG.htm ('You cannot change a recovery Org vDC for an existing VPG'); Provider vDC 'highest supported hardware version' check = VMware Cloud Director behaviour, not from Zerto docs

VPG0042.title: Failover or test network for VMs no longer exists
VPG0042.meaning: 'Recovery network not found' (Error). The Failover/Move or Failover Test network configured for the listed VMs does not exist, for example because an Org vDC network was deleted or renamed.
VPG0042.fix: Restore the network in vCD, or edit {vpg}'s NIC settings to choose existing failover and test networks. Agree the choice with the customer.
VPG0042.caution: Until this is fixed, recovering or testing these VMs has no valid network.
VPG0042.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0042.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/From_vCD_To_vCD_Define_NICs.htm

VPG0049.title: VPG auto-paused: protected VM missing from inventory
VPG0049.meaning: 'Protection group missing VM' (Error). Zerto paused the VPG because one or more protected VMs disappeared from the hypervisor inventory. Checkpoints are kept, and all VMs, including the missing ones, can still be recovered while the VPG is paused. No new checkpoints are written until it is resolved.
VPG0049.fix: Find out what happened to {vm} on the protected site (for inbound VPGs, the customer's vCenter) and return the VM or its host to the inventory; replication then resumes. Only if the VM is gone for good, and with the customer's agreement, use Edit VPG to remove it, answering Yes to keep its replica disks.
VPG0049.caution: Once removed from the VPG, the VM can no longer be recovered. Answering No deletes its recovery volumes. The whole VPG stays paused, and its RPO keeps growing, until this is resolved.
VPG0049.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0049.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Removing_Protected_Virtual_Machines_from_the_Hypervisor_Inventory.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Removing_Virtual_Machines_from_a_VPG.htm

VPG0050.title: Several VPGs missed their failover-test schedule
VPG0050.meaning: 'Protection Group Tested Alert' (Warning). A summary alert listing VPGs that had no failover test in the last N months, or none at their configured testing time.
VPG0050.fix: Pass the listed VPGs to their customers or account owners and schedule Failover > Test runs on isolated test networks. Stop each test and record the result.
VPG0050.caution: Use Failover Test, never Failover Live or Move. Don't snapshot, delete or migrate the test VMs. Testing many VPGs at once uses scratch-journal storage on the recovery datastores.
VPG0050.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0050.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-10-25); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/The_Failover_Test_Operation.htm

VPG0051.title: Stopping a failover test failed
VPG0051.meaning: 'Stopping Failover Test Operation Failed' (Error). Zerto cannot finish stopping the VPG's failover test. Zerto lists four causes: problems with the recovery or protected hypervisor, storage, VRA or host availability, or the network between the sites.
VPG0051.fix: Fix the failing component (vCenter/vCD reachability, the recovery datastore, the VRA and its host, the site link), then retry Stop from {vpg} > Running Tasks. If it still fails, open a Zerto Support case.
VPG0051.caution: Don't delete, migrate or snapshot the 'testing recovery' VMs or their disks by hand; they run on the VRA-managed recovery disks.
VPG0051.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0051.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-01-10); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/What_Happens_After_Starting_a_Test.htm

VPG0052.title: Rolling back a Failover Live failed
VPG0052.meaning: 'Rolling back Failover Live Operation Failed' (Error). Zerto cannot complete the rollback of a Failover Live. The documented causes are the same as VPG0051: hypervisor, storage, VRA or host availability, or the inter-site network.
VPG0052.fix: Fix the failing component, then retry the rollback from {vpg} > Running Tasks. If it still fails, open a Zerto Support case.
VPG0052.caution: Don't switch to Commit to 'get past it' without the customer's decision. Don't delete recovered VMs or VRA-attached disks by hand.
VPG0052.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0052.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-01-10); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Monitoring_a_Single_VPG.htm

VPG0053.title: Rolling back a Move failed
VPG0053.meaning: 'Rolling back Move Operation Failed' (Error). Zerto cannot complete the rollback of a Move. The documented causes are the same as VPG0051: hypervisor, storage, VRA or host availability, or the inter-site network.
VPG0053.fix: Fix the failing component, then retry the rollback from {vpg} > Running Tasks. If it still fails, open a Zerto Support case.
VPG0053.caution: Don't Commit instead without the customer's decision: committing a Move removes the source VMs, and without reverse protection it deletes the source disks. Don't delete moved VMs or VRA-attached disks by hand.
VPG0053.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0053.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-01-10); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Committing_the_Move_Operation.htm

VPG0055.title: Recovery volume size doesn't match the protected volume
VPG0055.meaning: 'VPG Not Correctly Configured for Protected Volume Size' (Error). A protected volume was resized and the ZVM could not update the VPG to match, so the recovery and protected volume sizes now differ for the VM.
VPG0055.fix: Edit {vpg} and click Done without changing anything. This is Zerto's documented fix; it makes the ZVM re-apply the volume sizes.
VPG0055.caution: Zerto synchronizes the VPG after the update if required, so a sync may follow.
VPG0055.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0055.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-01-10); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Editing_a_VPG.htm

VPG0057.title: Elastic Org vDC has an invalid Provider vDC configuration
VPG0057.meaning: 'Elastic VDC - invalid PVDC configuration' (Error). The Provider vDC behind the VPG's elastic Org vDC has changed to a configuration Zerto rejects. Zerto's documented cause is a new resource pool added under the Provider vDC on the same cluster.
VPG0057.fix: Review recent resource-pool changes on that Provider vDC with the vCD admins. Per Zerto, move the newly added resource pool to another cluster.
VPG0057.caution: Provider vDC changes affect every Org vDC and tenant on it, so plan the change. Don't edit or re-create the VPG to work around this.
VPG0057.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0057.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-01-10)

VPG0058.title: Recovery storage policy points at an unreachable datastore
VPG0058.meaning: 'Storage profile is not reachable' (Warning). A vCD storage policy used by the VPG resolves to a datastore that Zerto cannot reach; the datastore is identified by its vCenter MoRef, for example datastore-57999. Zerto gives two reasons: the datastore no longer exists, or it is not in the recovery cluster. Likely triggers are a retired or unmounted datastore, a host added to the cluster without it, or a storage-policy or tag change. Zerto 10.x documents the message as 'The VCD storage profile {datastore} is not reachable'; the estate prints 'The datastore ... is not reachable'.
VPG0058.fix: Resolve the MoRef in vCenter (https://<vCenter>/mob/?moid={datastore}, or PowerCLI Get-Datastore -Id Datastore-{datastore}) and check that every host in the recovery cluster mounts it, including hosts in maintenance mode (KB 3511). Fix it at the storage layer: re-present the datastore to the whole cluster or, if it was retired, take it out of the backing vSphere storage policy (tags or rules) or datastore cluster so the vCD policy resolves only to valid datastores. Check Setup > Datastores (Workload Protection view) for recovery or journal volumes still on it.
VPG0058.caution: Don't fix this by changing the VPG's storage policy or a VM's recovery datastore: Zerto states that changing the datastore in Edit VM puts the VPG through an initial sync. If recovery or journal volumes were on a datastore that is gone, treat it as a recovery-storage incident and open a Zerto Support case. Storage-policy changes, in vSphere or vCD, affect every tenant that uses that policy.
VPG0058.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0058.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-01-10); KB 000003511 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/3511.html; Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Managing_Protection_When_the_Recovery_Datastore_Will_Be_Unavailable_Datastore_Maintenance.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Monitoring_Datastores_The_SETUP_Tab_The_DATASTORES_Tab.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/ConfigureProvidervDCs.htm

VPG0059.title: Org vDC network settings corrupted in vCD
VPG0059.meaning: 'Corrupted Org vDC network' (Warning). An Org vDC network used by the VPG has corrupted settings in vCD.
VPG0059.fix: Fix the network in vCD, or edit {vpg} to use a different recovery network.
VPG0059.caution: Confirm the target network with the customer before changing the VPG.
VPG0059.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0059.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-01-10)

VPG0060.title: A disk was detached from a protected VM
VPG0060.meaning: 'VolumeDetach' (Warning). A volume was removed from the protected VM. It stays recoverable only while the journal still holds checkpoints from before the detach, and only if no other volume was added at the same location. The alert is deleted automatically once those checkpoints age out.
VPG0060.fix: Confirm with the customer that removing the disk from {vm} was intended. If it was not, act while a checkpoint from before the detach is still in the journal: Offsite Clone the VM to that checkpoint (VPGs tab > three-dot menu > Offsite Clone > Advanced to pick {vm} > Select a Checkpoint) and give the customer the recovered disk. On a vCD recovery site the clone is created in vCenter and has to be imported into vCD.
VPG0060.caution: Once those checkpoints age out of the journal (which is also when the alert clears), Zerto can no longer recover the volume. The clone is an unprotected full copy on recovery storage that keeps the source MAC/IP settings: don't power it on where it can clash with production, and delete it when done, because Zerto notes a leftover clone can stop VMs powering on in a later failover.
VPG0060.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0060.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-01-10); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Cloning_VPG_to_the_Recovery_Site.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/The_Clone_Operation.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/The_Failover_Live_Process.htm

VPG0061.title: Protected vCD vApp looks corrupted in vCD
VPG0061.meaning: 'VpgVappBrokenReflection' (Warning). The VPG protects a vApp whose data in vCD appears corrupted; the message asks you to make sure all vApp VMs are powered on and running. Zerto's documented cause is 'a protected broken vCD vApp in old ZVM version'. It applies only where a vCD site is the protected side, for example provider-to-provider VPGs.
VPG0061.fix: In vCD, check the vApp: all member VMs are present, powered on and running, and the vApp is not in a failed state. Fix it there and see whether the alert clears; if it persists, open a Zerto Support case.
VPG0061.caution: Zerto's listed resolution for this code is copied from VPG0059's network text, so treat it as unreliable. Don't delete or re-create the VPG to clear the alert.
VPG0061.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0061.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-01-10)

VPG0063.title: VPG references a ZORG the ZVM no longer knows
VPG0063.meaning: 'The ZORG of the VPG was not found in the storage' (Error; Zerto 10.x and later). The VPG refers to a ZORG that does not exist for this ZVM. Zerto's documented cause is that the ZCM holding the ZORG was forcibly detached from the ZVM.
VPG0063.fix: In ZCM > Sites, confirm that this ZVM is still attached and that the ZORG still exists. If the ZCM was replaced, recreate the ZORG in the new ZCM and edit {vpg} to reference it; this is Zerto's documented fix.
VPG0063.caution: Don't delete and re-create the VPG to clear the alert: that discards the journal and forces a new sync of the whole VPG.
VPG0063.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0063.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-01-10)

VRA0001.title: Host in a VRA cluster has no VRA installed
VRA0001.meaning: Host {host} is in cluster {cluster}, where other hosts have VRAs, but has no VRA itself. Replication is not affected now. However, any protected VM that is vMotioned or DRS-moved onto this host stops protection for its whole VPG, and the host cannot act as a recovery host. Zerto requires a VRA on every host that runs protected VMs or that VMs may recover to, and recommends one on every host in the cluster.
VRA0001.fix: If {host} can run protected VMs or receive recovered VMs, install a VRA: Setup > VRAs > select {host} > NEW VRA. Give it a static IP with the same subnet mask and default gateway as the other VRAs in {cluster}. If {host} is deliberately left without a VRA (being built or retired), keep protected VMs off it (for example with a DRS rule) until that changes.
VRA0001.caution: The install dialog and the cluster default VRA settings pre-fill Subnet Mask 255.255.255.0. Enter the real mask: a /24 on a /23 network silently breaks ZVM-VRA comms (ZVM0002). 'Populate VRA Post Installation' may already be ticked, because its default follows Site Settings > Workload Automation > 'Enable VRA auto population after installation'; untick it unless you mean to move recovery volumes onto the new VRA, because populating can trigger a delta sync. Never reuse an IP that an old or ghost VRA VM still holds: duplicate VRA IPs crash-loop the peer VRAs (KB 4893). On a ZCM cloud site, customers' VRAs reach each cloud VRA through 2 ports on their Cloud Connector, so confirm the connector firewall rules allow the new VRA's ports.

VRA0024.title: VRA deleted outside Zerto, leaving a ghost VRA
VRA0024.meaning: A VRA or shadow VRA (VRA-H) was removed from vCenter while it still managed recovery disks, so Zerto shows it as 'Ghost VRA' (GET /v1/vras flags it as isGhost). KB 4246 lists other triggers: the host was removed from vCenter and re-added (new MoRef; Zerto 10.x tries to re-map these), a recovery or journal disk was detached from the VRA, or a failover-test VM was deleted. Replication stops for every VPG listed, and those VPGs show an error state. The estate sample has a blank host and an empty VPG list, which probably means an orphan with no VPGs; verify before acting.
VRA0024.fix: In Setup > VRAs, find the VRA whose status is 'Ghost VRA' and check its # VPGs; for a source-side ghost, vMotion the VMs it protects to other VRA hosts until # VPGs is 0 (KB 4246). Once # VPGs is 0, uninstall it from the Zerto UI (not from vCenter) and reinstall a VRA if the host stays in service. If VPGs still recover to it, open a Zerto Support case before changing anything: the documented fix deletes those VPGs keeping the recovery disks, reinstalls the VRA, and recreates the VPGs from the preseeded disks.
VRA0024.caution: Deleting and recreating a VPG discards all its journal checkpoints and forces a resync; preseeding only reduces how much data is copied. Customer (ZORG) VPGs need customer sign-off, and the VPG settings must be recorded first. Always keep the target/recovery disks when deleting, and never delete the ghost VRA's disks from the datastore. Moving protected VMs off the ghost host also triggers a sync (bitmap or delta) for their VPGs. Don't give a new VRA an IP that a leftover VRA VM still holds (KB 4893). On a ZCM cloud site, a reinstalled VRA does not get its old Cloud Connector ports back; new ports must be opened in the firewall before customers can replicate through it.

VRA0028.title: VRA VM is powered off
VRA0028.meaning: The VRA VM on {host} is powered off. Error means the host runs protected VMs or is a recovery host: those VPGs go to an error state and RPO grows until the VRA is back, after which VPGs recovering to it run a bitmap sync and protected VMs that kept running on the host need a delta sync (KB 4030). Warning (what the estate shows) means no VPGs use this VRA now, so there is no current impact, but VMs that move onto the host are unprotected. It is common during or shortly after host maintenance.
VRA0028.fix: If {host} has recently left maintenance mode, wait about a minute: by default the VRA powers itself on 30 s after exit. Otherwise power on the VRA VM (Z-VRA-{host}) in vCenter and give Zerto a few minutes to refresh; if it won't power on, investigate the host. If the alert remains 10-15 min after power-on, open a Zerto Support case with logs.
VRA0028.caution: Don't edit, snapshot, migrate or delete the VRA VM in vCenter: it is Zerto-managed and cannot be moved between hosts. After power-on, expect a bitmap sync (or a delta sync for protected VMs that stayed on the host), not an initial sync. If the host is meant to stay in maintenance, leave the VRA off.

VRA0032.title: Local VRA(s) running an outdated version
VRA0032.meaning: At least one VRA on this site is older than the VRA version that ships with the site's Zerto. This usually happens when 'Auto-Upgrade Virtual Replication Appliances' was not selected during the Zerto upgrade. Replication is not directly affected. Zerto supports VRAs at most one version behind the site's Zerto version. Paired sites also raise an alert (VRA0033) for the same VRAs.
VRA0032.fix: Plan a change window and upgrade in small batches: in Setup > VRAs, filter VRA Version = Outdated, select a few VRAs, then More > Upgrade > Upgrade Selected VRAs. Alternatively use Upgrade VRAs on the cluster row, which is the only option in a VAIO-variant cluster.
VRA0032.caution: Each VRA upgrade is followed by a bitmap sync on both sites for VPGs using that VRA, and they may briefly show Not Meeting SLA. VPGs recovering to the VRA cannot avoid this, and on a cloud site that is most of them. vMotioning protected VMs to another VRA host first only covers the protected side, and those VMs also bitmap-sync (KB 4030). Don't upgrade every VRA at once. In VAIO-variant clusters the I/O-filter upgrade needs each host in maintenance mode.

VRA0033.title: VRA(s) on a paired site running an outdated version
VRA0033.meaning: This site is reporting VRAs that belong to peer site {peer} and are not on the latest version, for example Z-VRA-esx01.example.com on Site-C. Both the outdated VRA and the fix are on the peer site. Replication is not directly affected.
VRA0033.fix: On {peer}'s ZVM: Setup > VRAs > select the VRA(s) named in the alert > More > Upgrade. If {peer} is a customer's own site, notify the customer, because the VRA is theirs to upgrade.
VRA0033.caution: The upgrade triggers a bitmap sync on both sites for VPGs that use that VRA. Schedule it with whoever owns {peer}.
VRA0033.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VRA0033.htm (Alarms/Alerts bundle 9.5-10.9, updated 2025-01-10); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Upgrading_VRAs.htm (Admin Guide vSphere v10.9: the alert is issued on the site with the old VRA and on every paired site)

VRA0039.title: Journal hit its hard size limit; history being trimmed
VRA0039.meaning: 'Journal reached configured limit' (Error). Zerto files it under VRA alerts, but it is per VM/VPG. The VM's journal has reached its Journal Size Hard Limit, so Zerto promotes older checkpoints to the recovery disks to make room. The actual journal history, and therefore the set of available recovery points, shrinks below the SLA, and per KB 4032 the VPG can drop into a bitmap sync. It usually follows VRA0040.
VRA0039.fix: Confirm with the customer why {vm}'s change rate rose (KB 4032) and check journal-datastore free space in Setup > Datastores. Then raise {vm}'s Journal Size Hard Limit in Edit VPG > Replication > VM Settings; VPG-level defaults don't change existing VMs. If {vpg} uses a non-Custom ZCM service profile, a provider ZCM admin adds one with a larger hard limit and the same or longer Journal History, assigns it to the ZORG (Organizations > {zorg} > Service Profiles), and {vpg} is edited to select it, agreed with the customer.
VRA0039.caution: Until this is fixed, the available recovery points cover less time than the SLA. Expect a sync after enlarging the journal: Zerto states that a journal that was full and then had its size increased requires a synchronization. Bigger journals consume recovery storage, and a journal datastore below min(30 GB, 15%) free blocks journal writes and raises RPO for every VPG on it. Don't set the limit to Unlimited on shared datastores without capacity headroom. A service-profile switch changes the SLA for the whole VPG, so make sure the new profile doesn't shorten Journal History, and check {vm}'s journal limits in VM Settings afterwards.

VRA0040.title: Journal grew past its size warning threshold
VRA0040.meaning: 'Journal space low' (Warning). Zerto files it under VRA alerts, but it is per VM/VPG and arrives with entity Vpg. The recovery-side journal for the VM has grown past its Journal Size Warning Threshold, expressed here as a percent of the protected VM's volume size (KB 3880 quotes the same 'exceeded 50 percent of the protected VM volumes size' wording). Replication continues (KB 4014). It is an early warning that the journal is heading for its hard limit (VRA0039). The usual cause is a jump in the VM's change rate, or a threshold that is too low for the configured journal history. For ZORG VPGs the percentages can come from the ZCM service profile, which defines journal limits as a percent of VM volume size.
VRA0040.fix: Check whether {vm}'s change rate jumped (ask the customer; KB 4014 suggests Zerto Analytics Planner) and how much free space the journal datastore has (Setup > Datastores). If the growth is legitimate, raise {vm}'s Journal Size Warning Threshold in Edit VPG > Replication > VM Settings, keeping it below the hard limit (raise the hard limit as for VRA0039 if the journal is close to it). If {vpg} uses a non-Custom ZCM service profile, the thresholds come from the profile, so a provider ZCM admin adds one with a higher threshold and the same or longer Journal History, assigns it to the ZORG (Organizations > {zorg} > Service Profiles), and {vpg} is edited to select it, agreed with the customer.
VRA0040.caution: The alert reference says to 'remove older checkpoints'; ignore that. Don't shorten Journal History or lower the hard limit to silence the alert either: all of these throw away recovery points. VPG-level journal settings apply only to VMs added later, so make the change on each VM; a service-profile switch changes the SLA for the whole VPG, so check {vm}'s limits in VM Settings afterwards. Zerto lists 'journal size changed' as a sync trigger, so a sync may follow. Journals are stored on the provider's recovery storage, and the ZORG Max Storage quota does not count journal disks. If a journal datastore drops below min(30 GB, 15%) free, Zerto blocks journal writes and RPO climbs for every VPG on that datastore.
VRA0040.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VRA0040.htm (Zerto Alarms, Alerts and Events - All Environments, bundle tagged 9.5-10.9, page updated 2025-01-10); KB 000004014 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4014.html and KB 000003880 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/3880.html (tagged 8.0-10.9); Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Editing_a_VPG.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Synchronization_Triggers.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Journal_Sizing.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/To_VCD_Define_Replication.htm (Service Profile sets VPG SLA; VM Settings per VM); ZCM Admin Guide 10.9 https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/AddServiceProfile.1.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/ZORGServiceProfiles.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/Adding_and_Editing_vCD_Resources.htm

VRA0050.title: VRA's stored ESXi root password no longer works
VRA0050.meaning: The VRA on {host} reaches the host with the ESXi root password ('Use credentials to connect to host') rather than VIB, and that password has changed. The ZVM checks the password once a day. Zerto KB 4589 says VPGs using that VRA will go into an error state, so treat this as affecting replication. The estate samples are customer hosts, so the fix belongs on the ZVM that manages {host}.
VRA0050.fix: On the ZVM that manages {host} (for a customer host, the customer's ZVM, so notify them): Setup > VRAs > select the VRA(s) > Actions > Change Host Password, enter the current ESXi root password, and Save. VRAs that share the same new password can be updated together.
VRA0050.caution: The other documented option, deselecting 'Use credentials to connect to host' to switch the VRA to VIB, needs the host acceptance level set to CommunitySupported and is not allowed on Secure Boot hosts, so on-call should only update the password. This fix only updates a stored credential: don't uninstall or reinstall the VRA, and don't edit or recreate VPGs.

VRA0056.title: VRA shutting down for host maintenance mode
VRA0056.meaning: {host} is entering maintenance mode. The VRA waits up to 10 min for protected VMs to vMotion away, then shuts down, and it powers back on 30 s (default) after the host exits maintenance. VMs that moved to other VRA hosts stay protected after a bitmap sync. Any VMs still on the host when the 10 min run out are unprotected until it returns, and their VPGs then need a delta sync (KB 4030). VPGs recovering to this VRA show an error until it is back, unless the host was evacuated first. The ZVM can also replay a stale maintenance event after reconnecting to vCenter and shut the VRA down although the host is not in maintenance (KB 3448).
VRA0056.fix: If vCenter shows {host} entering maintenance, no action is needed beyond confirming the VRA powers back on afterwards (if not, see VRA0028); evacuate recovery hosts before future maintenance (Setup > VRAs > Actions > Evacuate Host). If vCenter shows no recent maintenance task for {host}, it is likely a stale event replayed after a ZVM-vCenter reconnect (KB 3448): make sure the VRA comes back on and investigate why the ZVM lost vCenter.
VRA0056.caution: Evacuate Host moves recovery volumes and may trigger a delta sync. Site Settings > Workload Automation > 'Enable VRA auto evacuation once entering host maintenance mode' does this on every future maintenance, so change-control it rather than turning it on during on-call. Cancelling the maintenance-mode task stops the VRA shutdown from completing. After maintenance, DRS can move protected VMs back before the VRA is ready, causing delta syncs (KB 4919): set DRS to Manual or wait for the VRA to reconnect, and never disable DRS on a vCD cluster, because that deletes the resource pools behind the Org vDCs. If busy hosts keep hitting the 10-minute limit, Zerto Support can raise it (KB 4030).

VRA0063.title: VRA's VraMain service is down or crash-looping
VRA0063.meaning: The VRA VM on {host} is up, but its main service (VraMain) is down or crash-looping. With nothing listening on ports 4005-4009, the ZVM-VRA and VRA-VRA links drop. Error means VPGs protected by or recovering to this VRA have stopped replicating and their RPO is growing; Warning (the estate sample) means no VPGs use it now. Documented causes: a duplicate VRA IP, often held by a leftover or ghost VRA VM, which crash-loops every peer VRA (KB 4893); an invalid default gateway (KB 5120); and a full /mnt/log (KB 3143).
VRA0063.fix: Confirm the VRA VM is on, then SSH to it from the ZVMA shell (10.9 ZVMA guide 'Connecting to the VRA Over SSH'; KB 5108) and run 'ps -e | grep -i VraMain' (CPU time that keeps resetting means a crash loop) and 'df -h' (/mnt/log at 100%). Check that no other VM holds the VRA's IP and that its mask and gateway are valid. Collect VRA logs and open a Zerto Support case, which is Zerto's documented resolution.
VRA0063.caution: If many VRAs raise VRA0063 at once, suspect a duplicate VRA IP on a paired site (KB 4893); rebooting VRAs one by one will not fix it. Restarting VraMain or the VRA interrupts replication for every VPG on it, so do it only with Zerto Support. The bad-gateway case needs a VRA uninstall and reinstall: vMotion protected VMs off and evacuate recovery volumes first, and expect syncs. On a ZCM cloud site, the reinstalled VRA does not get its old Cloud Connector ports back; new ports must be opened in the firewall before customers can replicate through it.

ZVM0002.title: ZVM lost contact with a VRA (ports 4005/4006/4009)
ZVM0002.meaning: The ZVM cannot reach the VRA at {ip} on {host}. In 10.x the alert names the failing port: 4005 = log collection, 4006 = ZVM-VRA communication, 4009 = checkpoints. While it lasts, no new checkpoints are written for VMs whose recovery this VRA manages, VPGs drift to RPO or History Not Meeting SLA, and syncs such as bitmap syncs can stall. Causes: a Zerto upgrade in progress (transient); the VRA off or VraMain crashed; network, firewall or MTU problems; a DHCP-assigned VRA IP; a VRA IP overlapping the ZVMA's Kubernetes range; and a VRA subnet mask that differs from the other VRAs on its gateway, for example /24 on a /23 (seen in production at more than one site). Zerto's doc lists the severity as Error, but the estate reports Warning.
ZVM0002.fix: Confirm the VRA VM (and any VRA-H) is powered on with a static IP and that no Zerto upgrade is running; if {host} is a customer host (for example outside your own domain), these checks belong on the customer's ZVM, so notify them. Compare the VRA's Subnet Mask and Default Gateway with healthy VRAs on the same gateway (Setup > VRAs > select > Actions > Edit, or GET /v1/vras vraNetworkDataApi) and, if they differ (for example 255.255.255.0 on a /23), correct the mask and Save. If they match, run telnet {ip} on 4005, 4006 and 4009 and 'ping -M do -s <MTU-28> {ip}' from the ZVMA shell; if ping works but the ports refuse, troubleshoot as VRA0063.
ZVM0002.caution: Edit VRA network settings only while the VRA is powered on: per KB 4499, a change made while it is off reaches vCenter but not Zerto, and the VRA never reconnects. In Edit VRA, change only the network fields: changing VRA RAM or vCPU in the same dialog powers the VRA off. After a fix, Zerto can wait up to 15 min before resyncing, usually with a bitmap sync rather than a full sync. Don't uninstall the VRA or delete VPGs to fix connectivity.
