The mask-first check comes from field experience; KB 4787's 'correct any VRA network-settings mismatch' step supports it.

ZVM0003.title: Local ZVM lost connection to a paired site's ZVM (TCP 9071)
ZVM0003.meaning: 'No connection to site' (Error). Needs action if it lasts more than a few minutes. The local ZVM's link to the named peer ZVM (HTTPS, TCP 9071) is down. Zerto gives three causes: a brief resync after a failed recovery operation, a network problem on the way to the peer, or the peer's ZVM not running. For a customer (ZORG) peer, all traffic goes through that customer's Zerto Cloud Connector (ZCC), and the cloud ZVM reaches the ZCC on 9071, so a ZCC fault also raises this alert. While the link is down, no new VPGs can be created for that peer. If VRA traffic is cut as well (for example, the ZCC is down), replication stops, RPO grows, and the VPGs need a sync (for example, a bitmap sync) once the link is back.
ZVM0003.fix: If it lasts more than a few minutes, open the local ZVMA shell (VM console, or SSH if enabled; Appliance Manager option 0), run telnet {ip} 9071 against the address in the alert (KB 5107), and confirm the {peer} ZVM is running. For a customer peer, check that ZORG's connector in ZCM (Organizations > {zorg} > EDIT > Customer Sites, Status column) and that its Z-Connector VM is powered on in vCenter. Then have the customer test TCP 9071 from their ZVM to the ZCC and check their WAN and firewall (KB 4786).
ZVM0003.caution: Never unpair and re-pair to clear this alert. Unpairing deletes every VPG between the two sites, so journal history is lost and re-protecting needs a new initial or preseed sync. KB 4786's ZCC rebuild route (unpair, reinstall ZCC, re-pair, import VPGs) has the same effect. If the ZCC itself is broken, use ZCM Redeploy with Zerto Support instead, but expect Redeploy to drop that customer's link while it runs and their VPGs to resync afterwards. Restarting a ZVM (Appliance Manager option 3) or rebooting a ZCC, as KB 4786 suggests, interrupts replication; on a cloud ZVM that hits every tenant. ZVMA ICMP echo is off by default, so a failed ping to a ZVMA proves nothing; rely on the 9071 test.
ZVM0003.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/ZVM0003.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events, tagged 10.9, updated 2025-10-27); https://help.zerto.com/kb/000005107 (ZVMA-to-ZVMA, validated on 10.0 U2); https://help.zerto.com/kb/000004786 (with ZCC, tagged through 10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Unpair_Sites.htm (v10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Linux.ZVM.HTML.10.9/page/ZVM_Linux_Appliance_Menu.htm (v10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Linux.ZVM.HTML.10.9/page/DNS_Targets_Ports.htm (v10.9, 9071 = HTTPS between paired ZVMAs); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/RedeployCloudConnector.htm (ZCM v10.9); https://help.zerto.com/kb/000002897 (ZVM restart interrupts replication; tagged through 10.9)

ZVM0004.title: Informational: paired peer sites still on an older Zerto version
ZVM0004.meaning: 'Peer ZVM version out-of-date' (Warning). Informational: this site runs a newer major or minor release (here 10.9) than the peers listed in the alert. Zerto says the alert applies only when the newer version is a major or minor release, not an update. It does not stop replication by itself. It needs action only if a peer is outside the pairing matrix (10.9 pairs with sites up to two releases older or newer, meaning 10.8.x or 10.7.x, which is 10.0 U7), or if the gap blocks the next upgrade (see ZVM0007). Zerto's documented fix is to upgrade the peer sites.
ZVM0004.fix: No on-call action: in the Sites tab, add the Version column (configuration icon > Show/Hide Columns) and check each listed peer. Any peer older than 10.7 (10.0 U7) is outside 10.9's pairing window, so ask that customer to plan an upgrade. With the customer's agreement, the provider can also run it from Zerto Cloud Control (cloudcontrol.zerto.com) > Upgrade Manager for customers paired through a provider ZCC without a perpetual licence (it needs outbound 443 from the customer).
ZVM0004.caution: Don't unpair or re-pair to fix a version gap: unpairing deletes the VPGs. A peer upgrade restarts that peer's ZVM services, which briefly interrupts its replication. Upgrading its VRAs triggers bitmap syncs on both the protected and recovery sides of the affected VPGs, so the provider's recovery VRAs carry that load too. Treat any pushed customer upgrade as a planned change.
ZVM0004.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/ZVM0004.htm (tagged 10.9, updated 2025-10-27); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Pairing_Matrix.htm (v10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Monitoring_Peer_Sites_The_SITES_Tab.htm (v10.9, Version is an optional column); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Using_Upgrade_Manager.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Zerto_Cloud_Control_-_Overview.htm (v10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/RN.HTML.10.9/page/release_notes_for_hpe_zerto_10_9.html (10.9 GA, uses 10.7.x numbering); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Upgrading_VRAs_Procedure.htm (v10.9); https://help.zerto.com/kb/000002897

ZVM0006.title: Informational: newer Zerto release available for this site
ZVM0006.meaning: 'Upgrade available' (Warning). Informational; nothing is broken. A newer release can be installed on this site (here 10.9_U1, released as 10.9.10). Zerto's alert page gives the cause as the protected and recovery sites running different Zerto versions.
ZVM0006.fix: No on-call action; raise a planned change. Upgrade ZCM first, then each ZVMA from its Management Console (https://<ZVM>/management) > Appliance Upgrade after taking a snapshot of the ZVMA VM. Keep all provider sites on the same version and every paired peer within two releases, and include clearing any ZVM0007 blocker (outdated VRAs) in the same plan.
ZVM0006.caution: The ZVM services restart during the upgrade, and KB 2897 says a ZVM restart temporarily interrupts replication to and from that ZVM; on a cloud site that means every tenant. VRA upgrades (Auto-upgrade VRAs, or Setup > VRAs > More > Upgrade) trigger bitmap syncs on both the protected and recovery sides. Zerto's vSphere alarm doc says it will let you upgrade to a version that a paired peer cannot work with, so check customer peer versions first. Keycloak is upgraded too, so UI sessions are logged out.

ZVM0007.title: Informational: upgrade available but blocked by peer or VRA versions
ZVM0007.meaning: 'Cannot upgrade' (Warning). Informational, about upgrade readiness; current replication is not affected. The new release cannot be installed here yet. Either a paired peer runs a version the new release cannot work with, or a peer runs a higher version than this site (upgrade to the peer's version first), or VRAs on this site or a peer are on an older version.
ZVM0007.fix: No urgent action: in the ZVMA Management Console > Appliance Upgrade, open the version list (Start Upgrade, or Upgrade on the older layout) to see the stated blocker. In a change window, upgrade the outdated VRAs it (or VRA0032/VRA0033) names via Setup > VRAs > More > Upgrade on the site that owns them. If a peer runs a higher version, first upgrade this site to the peer's version; if a peer lags, get it upgraded (see ZVM0004).
ZVM0007.caution: Each VRA upgrade triggers a bitmap sync for the VPGs on that VRA, on both the protected and recovery sides. Zerto suggests removing affinity rules and vMotioning the protected VMs to another host with a VRA first, but that only covers the protected side, and the moved VMs also bitmap-sync (KB 4030). Upgrading this site's ZVM restarts its services, which briefly interrupts replication for every tenant on the site.

ZVM0011.title: ZVM cannot collect a host's metadata from vCenter
ZVM0011.meaning: 'Metadata collection' (Error). Needs action. The ZVM cannot collect the host's metadata, so VMs on that host cannot be protected and protected VMs cannot be recovered to it. KB 2897 calls it a VMware-side problem: vCenter is missing the host's configuration data (typically HostConfigInfo is empty in the vCenter MOB), so Zerto's view of the host is incomplete. Zerto's alert list shows which site issued each alert. Hosts outside your own domain (for example *.customer.example) are probably on a customer's own vCenter.
ZVM0011.fix: Confirm which site and vCenter own {host}; for a customer host, send the customer KB 2897. For a provider host, confirm it is Connected and open https://<vCenter>/mob/?moid=host-####: if HostConfigInfo is empty, cycle the host through maintenance mode, and reboot it only if that does not clear the alert. If the MOB data is complete, Zerto's cached view is stale and KB 2897's last step is a ZVM service restart, which must be a planned change.
ZVM0011.caution: Maintenance mode or a reboot shuts down the host's VRA, so follow Zerto's host-maintenance procedure first. Remove affinity rules and vMotion the protected VMs to another host with a VRA. Run Setup > VRAs > Actions > Evacuate Host for the VMs recovering to it (Zerto warns a delta sync may follow), then wait for syncs to finish. Skipping this means bitmap syncs and RPO breaches. Restarting the ZVM service (Appliance Manager option 3) interrupts all replication to and from that ZVM; on a cloud site that means every tenant.
ZVM0011.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/ZVM0011.htm (tagged 10.9, severity Error, updated 2025-10-27); https://help.zerto.com/kb/000002897 (all versions incl. 10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Managing_Protection_During_VMware_Host_Maintenance.htm (v10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Evacuate_Host_VRA_All_VMs.htm (v10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Alerts.htm (v10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Linux.ZVM.HTML.10.9/page/ZVM_Linux_Appliance_Menu.htm (v10.9)

ZVM0024.title: ESXi host disconnected from its vCenter
ZVM0024.meaning: vCenter reports {host} in cluster {cluster} at the named site as disconnected. Zerto lists only 'network problems' as the cause and does not document the effect on replication. ZVM-VRA and VRA-VRA traffic goes directly over IP, so replication may continue if the host and its VRA are still running, but Zerto cannot manage that host through vCenter until it reconnects. Check for companion ZVM0002 or VRA0063 alerts and the status of the VPGs on that host. The estate samples are customer sites.
ZVM0024.fix: In the vCenter of the named site (the customer's, if it is not a provider site), check {host}'s state, restore its management-network reachability, then right-click > Connection > Connect. Confirm the alert clears and the VPGs on {host} are back to Meeting SLA.
ZVM0024.caution: Don't remove {host} from the vCenter inventory and re-add it as a fix. Everything on it gets a new MoRef; Zerto 10.x tries to re-map these, which can take several minutes, but if that fails its VRA becomes a ghost VRA (VRA0024) and its VPGs stop replicating (KB 4246). If 'Enable VRA removal once host removed from inventory' is set, Zerto also uninstalls the VRA of a removed host that has no VPGs replicating to it. Reconnect the host instead.
ZVM0024.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/ZVM0024.htm (Alarms/Alerts bundle 9.5-10.9, page first published 2024, updated 2025-10-27); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Zerto_and_VMware_Features.htm ('Resiliency to vSphere Environment Changes', Admin Guide vSphere v10.9, updated 2026-06-17); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Automatically_Removing_VRAs_once_the_Host_is_Removed_from_the_Inventory.htm (Admin Guide vSphere v10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4246.html (KB 4246, All versions, updated 2021-08-09: a host re-added to vCenter creates a ghost VRA)

ZCC0001.title: Ghost Cloud Connector: customer's ZCC VM is gone, must redeploy
ZCC0001.meaning: 'Zerto Cloud Connector removed' (Error). Needs action. The Zerto Cloud Connector (ZCC) for customer {zorg} (cloud IP {ip}) no longer exists, for example because its host crashed or the VM was deleted, and ZCM lists it as a Ghost Cloud Connector. All of that customer's traffic goes through the ZCC, so their site is disconnected (ZVM0003) and replication into the provider stops until the ZCC is redeployed.
ZCC0001.fix: Check vCenter for the Z-Connector VM and the state of its host. Then in ZCM open Organizations > {zorg} > EDIT > Customer Sites, select the connector and click REDEPLOY (it reinstalls with the original IPs; pick a healthy host and datastore). Confirm the customer site reconnects and its VPGs finish syncing.
ZCC0001.caution: Use Redeploy. Don't remove and re-add the ZCC, and don't unpair: Zerto says a redeploy needs no VPG recreation or re-pairing, while unpairing deletes the VPGs. If the old ZCC VM could come back (for example, when a crashed host returns), keep it powered off, because the redeployed ZCC reuses its IPs (general practice, not in Zerto docs). Never snapshot ZCCs; Zerto says snapshots cause operational problems. Expect a sync (for example, a bitmap sync) of the customer's VPGs after they reconnect.

ZCC0002.title: Customer's Zerto Cloud Connector VM is powered off
ZCC0002.meaning: 'Zerto Cloud Connector powered off' (Error). Needs action. The customer's Zerto Cloud Connector (ZCC) VM is powered off. Zerto also lists a failed ZCC install as a cause, for example from vCenter problems, a full disk, network problems or wrong configuration. While the ZCC is off, the customer site paired through it is disconnected and its replication stops.
ZCC0002.fix: Power the Z-Connector VM back on in vCenter and find out why it stopped (host failure, full datastore, or a failed ZCM install or redeploy task). Confirm ZCM shows the connector healthy and the customer site reconnects (ZVM0003 clears).
ZCC0002.caution: Expect a sync (for example, a bitmap sync) on that customer's VPGs after they reconnect. Don't snapshot ZCCs. To move a ZCC, vMotion it instead of powering it off, and only shut it down if the target host has a different CPU; the target host needs the same VLANs and trunks.

ZCC0003.title: Orphaned Cloud Connector: ZVM cannot reach the customer's ZCC
ZCC0003.meaning: 'Orphaned Zerto Cloud Connector' (Warning). Needs action. The Zerto Cloud Connector (ZCC) VM exists but the cloud ZVM cannot connect to it. Zerto's causes: a network in its settings is invalid or unreachable; the IP, port group/VLAN or physical trunking behind the Cloud Network NIC is wrong; no route to the ZVM/VRA network (the ZCC's only default gateway sits on the Organization NIC, so a static route group is needed unless the ZVM and VRAs are on the cloud network); or the ports to the connector are blocked. If a newly deployed ZCC goes straight to orphaned, KB 4406 says the ZVM most likely cannot reach it on its Cloud Network NIC IP. The customer site behind this ZCC cannot connect.
ZCC0003.fix: From the cloud ZVMA shell, ping the ZCC's Cloud Network IP and test TCP 22 to it. Then check that NIC's port group/VLAN, physical-switch trunking, ARP entries and the connector's static route group (KB 4406). Only if the ZCC's own settings are wrong, replace it as a planned change: remove it in ZCM (Organizations > {zorg} > EDIT > Customer Sites) and add a new one with valid settings, reusing the Organization Network IP the customer pairs to.
ZCC0003.caution: Removing the ZCC keeps that customer disconnected until the replacement is up, and their VPGs will need a sync (for example, a bitmap sync) afterwards. Never unpair to rebuild it, because unpairing deletes the VPGs. If ZCM will not let you replace the ZCC without unpairing, stop and open a Zerto Support case. Don't edit the ZCC's iptables (KB 3138 warns this can cause severe issues), and don't snapshot ZCCs.
ZCC0003.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/ZCC0003.htm (tagged 10.9, updated 2025-10-25); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/Handling_an_Orphaned_Zerto_Cloud_Connect.htm, https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/Adding_a_Zerto_Cloud_Connector_For_a_Site.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/Resolving_Zerto_Cloud_Connector_Issues.htm (ZCM v10.9); https://help.zerto.com/kb/000004406 and https://help.zerto.com/kb/000003138 (KBs tagged through 10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Unpair_Sites.htm (v10.9)

status:Initializing.title: VPG being created and initially synchronized; not yet recoverable
status:Initializing.meaning: Status 0. Zerto's API reference defines it as: 'The VPG is being initialized. This includes when a VPG is created, and during the initial sync between sites.' Possible substatuses are Creating VPG, Syncing, Initial Sync, Volume Initial Sync and Full Syncing. No checkpoints exist yet, so the VPG cannot be recovered until the initial sync completes. The protected VMs must be powered on for the sync to progress.
status:Initializing.fix: No action while the progress % and throughput are moving. If it sits at 0% with no throughput, work it as cond:sync-stalled (powered-off VM, VRA or ZCC connectivity, throttling, storage).
status:Initializing.caution: These VMs have no DR until the sync completes, so don't report them as protected. Changing the recovery datastore or recreating the VPG restarts the initial sync from zero.

status:NotMeetingSLA.title: Both RPO and journal-history SLAs are being missed
status:NotMeetingSLA.meaning: Status 2. Zerto's API defines it as not meeting the SLA for both the journal history and the RPO. It is an umbrella status: Zerto normally pairs it with a substatus that names the cause, such as Delta Sync (not forced), Error, Needs Configuration, Recovery storage error, Site disconnection, VM not protected, or Volume Initial/Full Sync. Whether recovery is still possible depends on that substatus.
status:NotMeetingSLA.fix: Read the substatus and the VPG's alerts and fix that cause first (see the sub:* entries). If the substatus is None, treat it as RPO over target plus short journal history: find why checkpoints are late, then let the journal refill.
status:NotMeetingSLA.caution: Don't Force Sync or delete and recreate the VPG to clear the status. Force Sync starts a delta sync of the whole VPG. Deleting and recreating the VPG throws away every checkpoint and needs a new initial sync (only a delta sync if 'Keep the recovery disks at the peer site' was ticked and those disks are reused as preseeded volumes).
status:NotMeetingSLA.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Statuses.htm (Zerto 10.9 vSphere Admin Guide); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/API.ZVR.HTML/page/VPGs_API.htm (Zerto REST API ref, legacy 9.0-and-earlier: status enum 2); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Forcing_Sync_VPG.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Deleting_a_VPG.htm (10.9)

status:RpoNotMeetingSLA.title: Journal history OK, but RPO exceeds the Target RPO
status:RpoNotMeetingSLA.meaning: Status 3. The journal-history SLA is met, but actual RPO (seconds since the last checkpoint was written) is above the VPG's Target RPO. Zerto raises VPG0009 at 15-25% over target and VPG0010 at 25% or more. Documented causes are an IO burst (which clears by itself), a VRA bottleneck, a slow network or slow recovery storage. Any sync or site or VRA disconnection also stops checkpoints, so RPO keeps climbing.
status:RpoNotMeetingSLA.fix: Check the substatus and alerts first: a running sync or a disconnect (ZVM0002, VRA0005, ZVM0003) is the cause if present. Otherwise select our recovery VRA in Setup > VRAs: REMOTE MEMORY over 70% or CPU USAGE over 85% as an hourly average means it is saturated. Then check recovery datastore latency (over 40 ms; vCenter: VRA VM > Monitor > Performance > datastore) and WAN use against the bandwidth throttle on the protected site's ZVM (the customer's for inbound VPGs; time-based limits are in UTC).
status:RpoNotMeetingSLA.caution: Changing VRA RAM or vCPUs powers the VRA off and interrupts every VPG that uses it; they all resync afterwards. Go above 2 vCPUs, or change the Performance and Throttling advanced settings (IO throttling), only with Zerto Support. For inbound VPGs the protected VRA (its LOCAL MEMORY graph) is on the customer's ZVM, not in our Setup > VRAs.
status:RpoNotMeetingSLA.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Statuses.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0009.htm and /VPG0010.htm (Alarms, Alerts and Events ref, 9.5-10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Scale.Bench.Guide.HTML.10.9/page/guidelines_for_optimized_vra_topology_10_9.html (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Editing_VRA_Settings.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/PerformanceandThrottling.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4466.html (KB 4466, all versions: vCenter datastore-latency check)

status:HistoryNotMeetingSLA.title: RPO OK, but journal holds less history than configured
status:HistoryNotMeetingSLA.meaning: Status 4. The RPO SLA is met, but the journal holds less history than configured. There are two documented causes. (1) A recent sync: while a sync runs, old checkpoints age out and no new ones are added, so history stays short until the journal refills (VPG0003/VPG0004 clear automatically). (2) The journal reached its Journal Size Hard Limit, so Zerto promotes old data early and history stays short (VPG0037/VPG0038, or VRA0039 'has reached its configured limit').
status:HistoryNotMeetingSLA.fix: If a sync finished recently, wait: the status clears once the journal holds the configured history. If the journal hit its hard limit (VPG0037/VPG0038/VRA0039), raise the Journal Size Hard Limit per VM in Edit VPG > Replication > VM Settings > Edit Selected, because VPG-level journal settings apply only to VMs added later. If {vpg} uses a non-Custom ZCM service profile, its SLA settings are locked and in-use profiles can't be edited, so agree with the customer a move to a Custom profile (if the ZORG has one) or a new profile with a larger limit, assigned to {zorg} in ZCM and selected in Edit VPG.
status:HistoryNotMeetingSLA.caution: Zerto lists a journal-size change as a sync trigger, so expect a sync after saving. A bigger hard limit uses more recovery-site storage: if the journal datastore drops below 30 GB or 15% free (whichever is smaller), journal writes are blocked for every VPG on it, so check free space first. Don't move the journal to a non-default datastore as a quick fix; that forces an initial sync. After a service-profile switch, check the VMs' journal limits in VM Settings.
status:HistoryNotMeetingSLA.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Statuses.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0003.htm and /VPG0037.htm (alerts ref 9.5-10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Journal_Sizing.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Editing_a_VPG.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4032.html (KB 4032); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Synchronization_Triggers.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Configuring_Virtual_Protection_Groups.htm (10.9, service profiles); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.ZCM.HTML.10.9/page/AddServiceProfile.1.htm (ZCM 10.9: a service profile used by a VPG can't be edited); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/From_vCD_to_vCD_Define_Replication.htm (10.9: VM SETTINGS > EDIT SELECTED, service profiles)

sub:InitialSync.title: First full copy of protected disks; no recovery until done
sub:InitialSync.meaning: Substatus 1. The sync that runs after a VPG is created so the protected and recovery disks match. Recovery operations cannot run until it completes. The protected VMs must be powered on, because the VRA needs an active IO stack. Zerto gives three main reasons for a stuck initial sync: the protected VM is powered off, network problems between the VRAs, or insufficient resources (throttling, VRA resources, storage latency).
sub:InitialSync.fix: No action while it progresses. If it stalls, look for powered-off protected VMs (VRA0020) or protected VMs on hosts without a VRA, which the VM owner (the customer, for inbound VPGs) must power on, move to a VRA host or remove from the VPG. Then test VRA-to-VRA ports 4007/4008 (9007/9008 with VRA encryption; for a ZORG customer, the ZCC ports named in VRA0005), and check recovery datastore latency (Zerto throttles IO above 40 ms) and the bandwidth throttle on the protected site's ZVM (the customer's for inbound VPGs).
sub:InitialSync.caution: Don't recreate the VPG or change its recovery datastore to restart it: progress is lost and the initial sync starts over. Powering on, moving or removing a protected VM is the VM owner's decision; for inbound VPGs that is the customer.

sub:VolumeInitialSync.title: Full copy of one volume (new VM or disk, datastore change)
sub:VolumeInitialSync.meaning: Substatus 3. A full sync of a single volume. Typical triggers: a VM added to the VPG without a preseeded disk, a changed target datastore, a deleted recovery volume replaced with a new one, or a recovery volume switched between thin and thick. When the sync is for newly added VMs, the VMs already in the VPG stay recoverable, and each new VM becomes recoverable only once its sync completes.
sub:VolumeInitialSync.fix: No action while it progresses. If it stalls, check that the protected VM is powered on, the recovery datastore has space (VRA0012) and the VRAs can reach each other, as for cond:sync-stalled.
sub:VolumeInitialSync.caution: Every further datastore or thin/thick change on that volume restarts its initial sync. If the sync re-creates a volume of an existing VM (a replaced deleted volume or a recovery-datastore change), no new checkpoints are written and the VPG can't be recovered until the sync finishes.

sub:RecoveryPossible.title: Protected site unreachable; protection halted, failover still possible
sub:RecoveryPossible.meaning: Substatus 5 ('Recovery is possible'), shown on the recovery-site ZVM. Communication with the protected site's ZVM is down, so protection is halted, but this site can still recover to the last checkpoint. The protected side shows 'Site disconnection' instead. Zerto also shows it after a rollback, and when a failover is needed during a bitmap sync. For inbound customer VPGs it means the customer's ZVM or WAN is down, or our Zerto Cloud Connector (ZCC) for that ZORG is.
sub:RecoveryPossible.fix: Check the peer link: ZVM0003, {peer}'s status on the Sites tab, and telnet from the ZVMA to the peer address and port shown in ZVM0003 (9071). For a ZORG customer, confirm the ZCC for {zorg} is powered on (ZCC0002); a powered-off ZCC disconnects the paired site. If the customer's ZVM or WAN is down, contact the customer; the status clears on reconnect, usually followed by a sync.
sub:RecoveryPossible.caution: Don't fail over from here unless the customer declares a disaster: if the protected VMs are still running, you end up with two live copies. No new checkpoints arrive while the sites are disconnected.

sub:DeltaSync.title: Checksum resync of disks that should already match
sub:DeltaSync.meaning: Substatus 6. Zerto compares the protected and recovery disks by checksum and sends only the differences. Triggers: a protected host restarted without its VMs vMotioned off (including maintenance mode where the VRA's 10-minute evacuation wait expired), a VM vMotioned to a host without a VRA and back, some protected-side VRA upgrades, a preseeded disk, reverse protection after a failover or a Move (a vSphere-to-vSphere Move normally gets a bitmap sync instead), or Force Sync. No new checkpoints are written during it. Recovery to the last checkpoint is still possible, but Move is not.
sub:DeltaSync.fix: No action while progress moves. If it is stuck, check that the protected VMs are powered on, that VRA-to-VRA ports 4007/4008 (9007/9008 with encryption; for a ZORG, the ZCC ports named in VRA0005) are open both ways, and that storage latency is under 40 ms (KB 4477). To prevent repeats after host maintenance, set DRS to Manual until the host's VRA is back up, then vMotion the VMs back (KB 4919).
sub:DeltaSync.caution: Don't Force Sync a running delta sync; it only starts another one. Set DRS to Manual, never disable it: on a vCD cluster, disabling DRS deletes the resource pools that back the Org vDCs. If the sync will outlast the journal history, checkpoints age out until none remain, so take an Offsite Clone from the last good checkpoint first if recovery must stay possible; in vCD the clone lands in vCenter on the datastore with the most free space and must be imported into vCD.
sub:DeltaSync.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Statuses.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4477.html (KB 4477); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Managing_Protection_During_VMware_Host_Maintenance.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4030.html (KB 4030); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4919.html (KB 4919); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0007.htm (alerts ref 9.5-10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Reverse_Protection_For_a_Moved_VPG.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/From_vCD_to_vCD_Define_Replication.htm (10.9: disabling DRS removes all resource pools); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Cloning_VPG_to_the_Recovery_Site.htm (10.9: vCD clones created in vCenter); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VRA0005.htm (alerts ref 9.5-10.9)

sub:NeedsConfiguration.title: VPG settings missing or invalid; Edit VPG needed
sub:NeedsConfiguration.meaning: Substatus 7. One or more VPG settings are missing (alert VPG0006, 'missing configuration details'). Documented causes: a protected disk resize failed; a VM or volume was added with no matching recovery storage or not enough room; a VPG update was missed during a site disconnection or vCenter error (this can self-correct after reconnect); a Failover or Move was done without reverse protection; or a recovery Org vDC network was removed. It also happens when a protected VM acts as a backup proxy whose hot-added disks come and go (KB 3749).
sub:NeedsConfiguration.fix: Restore any site or vCenter disconnection first; that case can clear by itself after reconnect. Then open Edit VPG on {vpg} (from either site), step through the wizard, fill in the missing storage or Org vDC network and click Done. If it follows a Failover or Move done without reverse protection, leave the choice (configure reverse protection or remove the VPG) to the customer.
sub:NeedsConfiguration.caution: Configuring reverse protection replicates the recovered VMs back over the original protected VMs' disks where they still exist (delta sync), so it is the customer's failback decision; after a Move without reverse protection those disks were deleted, so it needs a full initial sync. Removing and re-adding a VM (or recreating a one-VM VPG, per KB 3749) discards that VM's recovery points and needs a fresh initial sync unless you keep its recovery disks and reuse them as preseeded volumes. Changing a volume's datastore or thin/thick type re-runs that volume's initial sync.
sub:NeedsConfiguration.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Troubleshooting_Needs_Configuration.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0006.htm (alerts ref 9.5-10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/3749.html (KB 3749); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Configuring_Virtual_Protection_Groups.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Removing_Virtual_Machines_from_a_VPG.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Reverse_Protection_For_a_Moved_VPG.htm (10.9: reverse sync uses the original protected disks); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Committing_the_Move_Operation.htm and https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Reverse_Protection_Not_Specified.htm (10.9: source disks deleted after a Move without reverse protection)

sub:Error.title: Protection broken; VPG not recoverable until cause fixed
sub:Error.meaning: Substatus 8, a generic error: Zerto cannot continue protection. Examples: the ZVM is disconnected from a VRA protecting or recovering the VPG's VMs (including a recovery VRA shut down for host work), or a volume connected to a VM in the VPG was deleted. Per Zerto, the VPG cannot be recovered until the problem is resolved. Storage errors, missing disks and site disconnections have their own substatuses.
sub:Error.fix: Read the VPG's alerts. For a VRA problem, power the VRA on (VRA0028), open a Zerto Support case for a down VRA service (VRA0063), or work ZVM0002 as cond:on-disconnected-vra; the VPG then bitmap-syncs back to Meeting SLA by itself. For a deleted volume, set the empty Recovery Volume Location in Edit VPG > Storage (preseeded volume = delta sync, new volume = volume initial sync), or, with the customer's agreement, remove that VM in the VMs step.
sub:Error.caution: Recovery operations are blocked while the VPG is in Error, and stay blocked during a new volume's initial sync (a preseeded volume's delta sync keeps recovery possible). A VM removed from the VPG can no longer be recovered; choose Yes to keep its recovery disks. Don't delete and recreate the VPG unless Zerto reports it unresolvable (VPG0005) or Support tells you to: that discards all checkpoints and needs a new initial sync unless the recovery disks are kept and preseeded.

sub:VolumeDeltaSync.title: Checksum resync of a single volume
sub:VolumeDeltaSync.meaning: Substatus 12 ('Delta syncing a volume'). A delta (checksum) sync limited to one volume, for example a volume added to a protected VM using a preseeded disk. No new checkpoints are written during it. Recovery to the last checkpoint is still possible, but Move is not.
sub:VolumeDeltaSync.fix: No action while it progresses. If it stalls, run the same checks as for a delta sync: protected VM powered on, VRA-to-VRA ports open, storage latency under 40 ms (KB 4477).
sub:VolumeDeltaSync.caution: Don't Force Sync over it; that starts a delta sync of the whole VPG. Journal history shrinks while it runs.

sub:BitmapSync.title: Catch-up after a replication interruption; normally clears itself
sub:BitmapSync.meaning: Substatus 23. When the protected VRA can't deliver data, it records the changed areas in an in-memory bitmap and sends them once the cause clears. Documented causes: a WAN outage or overload (lowest-priority VPGs go first), recovery storage congestion, a recovery VRA that went down and rebooted (for example during a Zerto upgrade), or a full VRA buffer. It is also normal after vMotion or host-maintenance evacuation, Resume after Pause, Change VM Recovery VRA, and vSphere-to-vSphere reverse protection after a Move. No new checkpoints are written during it, but recovery to the last checkpoint stays possible. Zerto treats repeated bitmap syncs of over 1 minute with no fault as a sign the VRA is likely saturated.
sub:BitmapSync.fix: No action while it progresses after a known event (VRA restart or upgrade, host maintenance or vMotion, WAN blip, resume). Escalate as sub:BitmapSync-stalled if progress stops, if it keeps re-triggering with no such event, or if it is running toward the VPG's journal-history length.
sub:BitmapSync.caution: Don't Force Sync it: that replaces a cheap bitmap catch-up with a delta sync of the whole VPG. A bitmap sync that outlasts the journal history can lose all checkpoints. If Replication Pause Time is set (Site Settings > Policies), Zerto pauses the sync before the last checkpoints go (VPG0007) so you can take an Offsite Clone; in vCD the clone lands in vCenter on the datastore with the most free space and must be imported into vCD.

sub:BitmapSync-stalled.title: Bitmap sync frozen, never finishing, or constantly re-triggering
sub:BitmapSync-stalled.meaning: Not a Zerto substatus; this is the stuck case Zerto's KBs describe. The bitmap sync never completes, sits at 0% ('0 out of 0 GB') or 100% with no movement, or flips between Bitmap Sync and Meeting SLA, and no new checkpoints are written. Zerto attributes it to an environmental fault (blocked VRA-to-VRA or ZCC traffic, a ZVM-to-VRA disconnect) or too few resources (VRA CPU or RAM, bandwidth or throttling, storage latency, backup windows). Field experience: a VRA whose subnet mask differs from the others on its gateway (/24 on a /23) breaks ZVM-to-VRA comms and strands bitmap syncs (seen at more than one site).
sub:BitmapSync-stalled.fix: Test comms both ways: from the ZVMA, ping -M do -s <MTU-28> and telnet the VRA on 4005/4006/4009; from the VRA (SSH from the ZVMA, KB 5109), test the peer VRA on 4007/4008 or 9007/9008 (for a ZORG, the ZCC ports named in VRA0005). Fix any VRA mask mismatch in Setup > VRAs > Actions > Edit; if comms are clean, check our recovery VRA's REMOTE MEMORY (over 70%), CPU (over 85%) and vCenter NIC use (over 80%), datastore latency (over 40 ms), protected-site throttling and backup windows. If several VPGs on one VRA are frozen, open a Zerto Support case before rebooting any VRA.
sub:BitmapSync-stalled.caution: Rebooting a VRA, or changing its RAM or vCPU (which powers it off), interrupts every VPG that uses it, and a protected-side VRA restart or upgrade may turn bitmap syncs into delta syncs. Edit VRA network settings only while the VRA is powered on: per KB 4499, a change made while it is off reaches vCenter but not Zerto, and the VRA never reconnects. Don't Force Sync. If the stall may outlast the journal history, take an Offsite Clone from the last checkpoint first; in vCD it lands in vCenter and must be imported into vCD.

sub:RecoveryStorageError.title: I/O error writing to recovery-site storage
sub:RecoveryStorageError.meaning: Substatus 30. An I/O error on the recovery storage. Zerto's examples: the datastore is almost full (VRA0012 fires below 30 GB or 15% free, whichever is smaller), or 'the virtual machines are turned off and the recovery disks are inaccessible'. Writes to that storage stop and RPO climbs, and Zerto requires a sync once the storage problem is fixed. Related alerts: VRA0011, VRA0012, VRA0013, and VPG0058 (vCD storage profile not reachable).
sub:RecoveryStorageError.fix: Find the storage: VRA0012/VRA0013 name the recovery disk and VM, VPG0058 names the vCD storage profile, and for inbound ZORG VPGs it is on our side. Grow that datastore (Zerto's VRA0012 action) or free space on it so it stays above the smaller of 30 GB or 15% free, or restore its access from the recovery VRA's host. The VPG syncs once writes succeed.
sub:RecoveryStorageError.caution: Re-pointing the VPG to another recovery datastore triggers an initial sync of those volumes and resets the journal, with no recovery possible until it finishes, so treat it as a last resort. Don't svMotion the VRA's recovery or journal disks to make room: while they migrate, VPGs on that VRA can't fail over.

cond:sync-stalled.title: Sync at 0% with no data moving
cond:sync-stalled.meaning: Monitor-derived: a syncing substatus (Initial, Volume Initial, Delta, Volume Delta, Bitmap, Syncing or Creating) at 0% progress with under 0.5 MB/s throughput. A few minutes at 0% when a sync starts is normal; 'Syncing' means Zerto is still choosing the sync type. If it persists (30 minutes is a suggested local threshold, not a Zerto number), something is blocking it. Possible blockers: a powered-off protected VM, which halts the whole VPG (VRA0020); a VM on a host without a VRA (VPG0027); blocked VRA-to-VRA or ZCC traffic ('0 out of 0 GB'); a ZVM-to-VRA disconnect; VRA saturation or throttling; or storage latency.
cond:sync-stalled.fix: Start from the VPG's alerts: a powered-off protected VM (VRA0020) halts the whole VPG until its owner powers it on or removes it, and ZVM0002, VRA0005 or ZCC0002 mean broken comms. Test ZVMA-to-VRA on 4005/4006/4009 and VRA-to-peer on 4007/4008 (9007/9008 if encrypted; for a ZORG, the ZCC ports named in VRA0005) in both directions, and fix VRA mask mismatches in Setup > VRAs > Actions > Edit. Then check recovery datastore latency (over 40 ms) and bandwidth throttling on the protected site's ZVM (the customer's for inbound VPGs).
cond:sync-stalled.caution: Don't 'kick' it with Force Sync, VPG recreation or a recovery-datastore change: those restart the work as a delta sync or a fresh initial sync. Powering on or removing a protected VM is the VM owner's call (the customer, for inbound VPGs), and removing it ends its protection. Edit VRA network settings only while the VRA is powered on (KB 4499). Reboot VRAs only after the connectivity tests point there (KB 5109); every VPG on a rebooted VRA resyncs.

cond:no-recovery-point.title: RPO -1: no checkpoint, or RPO not yet calculated
cond:no-recovery-point.meaning: Monitor-derived: ActualRPO is -1 (or missing) while the VPG is not Initializing, Moving, FailingOver or Deleting. In Zerto's API, ActualRPO is the seconds since the last checkpoint, and '-1 means that the RPO has not been calculated'. Treat it as 'no recovery point' until proven otherwise. Documented ways a VPG ends up with no checkpoints: a sync that outlasts the journal history, 'Site disconnection. No checkpoints', a journal reset after re-pointing recovery storage, or an initial sync that never finished.
cond:no-recovery-point.fix: First rule out a VPG that was failed over or moved without reverse protection (it sits in Needs Configuration and isn't replicating; handle it with the customer). Otherwise confirm with GET /v1/vpgs/<vpg-id>/checkpoints/stats (earliest and latest); if no checkpoint exists, treat it as P1, clear the blocker shown in the substatus and alerts (stalled sync, disconnected peer, powered-off VM, storage error) so the sync can finish, and open a Zerto Support case if it won't move.
cond:no-recovery-point.caution: With no checkpoint there is no failover, test or clone for this VPG, so tell the customer. Avoid Force Sync and recovery-datastore changes for now; both restart or lengthen the sync and delay the first checkpoint.
cond:no-recovery-point.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/API.ZVR.HTML/page/VPGs_API.htm (REST API legacy ref: ActualRPO -1 = not calculated); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/VPG_Statuses.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/VPG0007.htm and /VPG0006.htm (alerts ref 9.5-10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/10.9_Swagger/page/index.html (10.9 API: /v1/vpgs/<id>/checkpoints/stats, earliest/latest); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Managing_Protection_When_the_Recovery_Datastore_Will_Be_Unavailable_Datastore_Maintenance.htm (10.9)

cond:rpo-over-target.title: Actual RPO above the VPG's Target RPO
cond:rpo-over-target.meaning: Monitor-derived: ActualRPO (seconds since the last checkpoint) is greater than ConfiguredRpoSeconds (the Target RPO). Zerto raises VPG0009 at 15-25% over target and VPG0010 at 25% or more. Documented causes are an IO burst (which clears by itself), a VRA bottleneck, a slow network or slow recovery storage. Any sync or disconnection also stops checkpoints. Zerto treats RPO over 5 minutes with no syncs running as a sign that the VRA is saturated.
cond:rpo-over-target.fix: If a sync or disconnect is in progress, fix that instead. Otherwise check our recovery VRA in Setup > VRAs (select it): REMOTE MEMORY over 70% or CPU USAGE over 85% (hourly average) means it is saturated, so plan a RAM increase or move VMs to another recovery VRA (Actions > Change VM Recovery VRA). Also check recovery datastore latency (Zerto throttles IO above 40 ms) and bandwidth throttling on the protected site's ZVM (the customer's for inbound VPGs; time-based limits are in UTC).
cond:rpo-over-target.caution: Changing VRA RAM or vCPU powers the VRA off and every VPG on it resyncs, so schedule it, and go above 2 vCPUs only with Zerto Support. Change VM Recovery VRA blocks edits, failover, test and clone on the affected VPGs while it runs and may end in a bitmap sync. For inbound VPGs the protected VRA is on the customer's ZVM, not in our Setup > VRAs. Raising the Target RPO only hides the alert.

cond:on-disconnected-vra.title: Protected VM's host VRA unreachable from its ZVM
cond:on-disconnected-vra.meaning: Monitor-derived: a VPG member's protected host is named in a ZVM0002 alert ('ZVM is not connected to VRA ... problem with port 4006/4009'). The ZVM talks to its local VRAs on 4005 (logs), 4006 (control) and 4009 (checkpoints). While it is cut off, checkpoints stop for the VMs that VRA handles, and the VPG typically goes to Error, which can't be recovered until resolved. Causes: a Zerto upgrade in progress, VRA powered off or crashed, a port block, a DHCP-assigned VRA IP, an IP overlapping the ZVMA's Kubernetes range, or (from field experience) a VRA mask that differs from the others on its gateway. The VRA install/edit default mask is 255.255.255.0, which is how /24 masks end up on /23 networks.
cond:on-disconnected-vra.fix: In Setup > VRAs, confirm the VRA on {host} is powered on, then from the ZVMA run ping -M do -s <MTU-28> {ip} and telnet {ip} on 4005/4006/4009. If its mask or gateway differs from the other VRAs on that gateway, correct it in Setup > VRAs > Actions > Edit (static IP). If {host} is a customer host, the fix is on the customer's ZVM, so notify them.
cond:on-disconnected-vra.caution: Don't uninstall and reinstall the VRA to fix comms: the VMs must be evacuated first, and a reinstalled VRA gets new Zerto Cloud Connector ports, which means firewall changes. Edit VRA network settings only while the VRA is powered on (KB 4499). Changing VRA RAM or vCPU powers the VRA off. During a Zerto upgrade, wait for it to finish. Expect bitmap syncs once comms return.
cond:on-disconnected-vra.source: https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Alarms.Alerts.HTML/page/ZVM0002.htm (alerts ref 9.5-10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4025.html (KB 4025); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/5108.html (KB 5108, 10.0 U2-U6); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/2970.html (KB 2970); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/z-kb-articles-zertokbs/page/4499.html (KB 4499, All versions, updated 2021-02-04); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Linux.ZVM.HTML.10.9/page/DNS_Targets_Ports.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Editing_VRA_Settings.htm (10.9); https://help.zerto.com/bundle/Admin.VC.HTML.10.9/page/Uninstalling_VRAs.htm (10.9); provider field experience (VRA mask incidents)
